recipes.name: Spicy Tuna Fish Cakes
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon dry breadcrumbs, or as needed
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place potato into a small pot and cover with salted water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and allow to steam dry in the pot for 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to a large bowl and mash with a potato masher or fork.

Add tuna, onion, egg, mustard, bread crumbs, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper and mix until well blended. Divide tuna mixture into eight equal portions and shape into patties.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add tuna patties and pan-fry until browned and crisp, about 3 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Tuna Fish Cakes
raw_recipe.description: These spicy tuna fish cakes are made with canned tuna, dried spices, onion, and a mashed potato for a binder. They fry up into deliciously crisp patties!

video.description: See how to make spicy tuna cakes using basic ingredients commonly found in the pantry.

review.reviewBody: Raquel these were super yummy! The only thing that I did change was I used saltines instead of bread crumbs because I was out and too lazy to make some. I love the addition of potato, it gave the cakes a great flavor! These were super simple and quick to make. Thanks for a great recipe that I will continue to use.

Giving this 5 stars --- because of the minor changes that I made.
I used Albacore Tuna, and only used 3 cans bc it's meatier than regular tuna.
I sauteed the onion with the Italian seasoning until the onion was tender.
Also, I microwaved the potato in a mcrwv-safe bowl for 5 mins! (Perfect!)
Lastly, I felt that I needed more olive oil to cook the patties, but in the end, all was very good! I will make them again!

Substituted 3 cups frozen hash browns (that I defrosted for three minutes in the microwave) for the mashed potatoes, and added another egg. Served them on shredded cabbage with choice of two sauces: sour cream, lemon juice, and dill, or sour cream, sweet chili sauce, and Tajin. They were a hit and have been requested to be in our regular rotation.

I made as is but did half canned salmon, half canned tuna. It was a little bland so next time I'll add more spices. For this time though, I doused it in Frank's hot sauce so it cheered up considerably. Also, my patties didn't bind as well as the perfect ones in the video, so maybe next time I'll add another egg.

I've never put potato in this type of recipe before. I like it. I used mackerel instead of tuna and upped the onion and red pepper. It gives then a nice kick. Next time I will use more mustard. One tip, if you have trouble flipping them, they are too thin. I tried making them like a potato pancake. That didn't work well. Once I started making them thicker and let each side cook closer to 4 minutes, it was no problem.
My hubby likes tuna, I am not a big fan but I must say these were fabulous. Topped paddies with cheddar cheese and served on toasted buns slathered with Chef John’s Remoulade 2.0 sauce. Yum!
This recipe is now a staple in our house. I bake them instead of fry them and use Lick-The -Spoon Cilantro Jalapeno Aioli on top. I refrigerate them and eat one for lunch everyday. Delicious!!!!
I substituted the Italian seasoning with old bay seasoning and served with tarter sauce. I formed them into 8 patties and refrigerated for awhile before frying.

I LOVE this recipe and I have been making these for a couple years now and am just now getting around to putting my review up. I will admit, I am someone who reviews a recipe that I have modified so if you are unhappy with that, move on. I do not use the potato, nor the breadcrumbs - keeping it low carb. I substitute an extra egg and almond flour. They hold together well, and the taste is delicious! I come back again and again for a quick, inexpensive, and tasty dinner option. Thank you so much for this!
Delicious. I baked these until slightly brown on top instead of frying using parchment paper. I also doubled the recipe. These are great for lunch also.

This was really good. My kids ate it up. I followed the recipe for what I had. I didn’t have garlic powder so I used 3 garlic cloves, I didn’t have Dijon mustard so I used honey mustard, I used almond flour instead of bread crumbs, and I used a sweet potato instead of a white potato. It was really tasty and my five year old who is picky said this is sooo good. And he ate every crumb
Whole family enjoyed this. Will become a staple
I will make again to be sure, all the cakes disappeared - no refrigeration needed. Balanced spicy flavor.
Used 2 tins of tuna instead of 4. 2 medium potatoes instead of 1 large. Happy with how they turned out.
Giving the weight of the potato, rather than just saying "large", would be helpful and might prevent some of the reported "fails".

I enjoyed these at dinner tonite. I am gluten free, so skipped the egg. Used a little onion powder instead of onions cause I don't like onions. I think they were delicious. Of course, being from Arizona, I added extra spicy stuff cause the devil made me do it! Delicious way to use albacore. Thanks for the change of pace! I served them on toast and lettuce for an open face sandwich. Folks talked about sauce, but I didn't see any with the recipe...didn't need any either. Oh! mine held together great , so I'm puzzled why some folks' patties didn't. I even left things a bit chunky when I mashed the potatoes and albacore. Go figure! I think
Followed the recipe exactly. Terrible. Falling apart in the skillet when you try to turn and taste blah.
I could not get it to hold together so now I have to figure out how to use it to not waste it.
Bad, We made it and it didn't even hold together and broke down and it tasted so bad
This dish has just the right amount of spice to make a delicious lenten meal.
